correctness.rationale: The exact polygon counts follow from sign changes on the nine actual prism edges: with 0,1,2,3 crossed vertical edges the sections have 4,5,4,3 vertices, respectively. The three base dot products sum to zero and an explicit order of their absolute values reduces Haar averaging to one sextant. Conditional normal-angle integration has the exact arcsine antiderivative. Direct differentiation gives a strictly increasing optimizing function J with J(0)=0 and J(infinity)>1, proving a unique global maximum. Triangle frequency has a positive derivative and an explicit inverse. Independent edge-crossing Monte Carlo and quadrature checks were run from the actual standalone script. Limitations: excludes measure-zero nontransversal orientations; exact continuum proof is analytic, not numerical.

value.rationale: The orientation-only polygon-count distribution for a natural right equilateral triangular prism is a complete, explicitly parameterized geometric invariant; its pentagon frequency has a nontrivial unique maximum at an interior aspect ratio, and its triangle frequency identifies that aspect ratio exactly. This has a clear motivation in section geometry and stereological sampling; unlike a mere new numeric constant, the result supplies a closed law, an extremal theorem and a rigorous inverse formula. No claim is made for arbitrary-offset cuts or general prisms.
